rationale: Deployers must implement a risk management policy and program for high-risk AI systems. Risk Management Program: AI operationalizes AI-specific risk identification, treatment and review across the lifecycle, which is the statutory duty of reasonable care.

Deployers must complete an impact assessment before use and at least annually. AI Impacts identifies potential impacts on individuals and groups and documents mitigations, producing the required assessment record.

Consumers must be notified if an AI system is a substantial factor in a consequential decision. This control governs the external communication of AI use ensuring plain-language disclosures are provided before the decision is made.

The Act explicitly targets algorithmic discrimination. This control requires the definition of fairness metrics and the documentation of testing results to prove that the system does not disadvantage protected groups.

Deployers must publish a public statement summarizing the high-risk systems in use and how risks are managed. This control ensures that public-facing transparency artifacts are accurate up-to-date and legally defensible.

Deployers rely on developer documentation to complete their assessments. This control compels the organization to obtain and validate model cards and risk disclosures from vendors before onboarding high-risk tools.
The Act regulates consequential decisions. Accountability assigns a human owner with authority over each high-risk system so decisions are flagged for enhanced governance and human review.

Impact assessments and risk records must be retained for at least three years. AI Regulatory Compliance maintains the compliance evidence set and its retention so records are available to the Attorney General.

If a developer discovers their system caused discrimination they must notify the AG and deployers within 90 days. This control ensures the organization has a protocol to receive and act on these critical vendor notifications.
Deployers must let consumers appeal adverse decisions and correct errors. Reporting Channels provide the accessible route for consumers to challenge an outcome and have it reviewed.

A deployer that discovers its high-risk system caused algorithmic discrimination must notify the Attorney General within 90 days. Regulatory Reporting owns timely regulatory notifications with the required content.
